title: Prove a tile really does come away in your hand
goal: Three features shipped in one day rest on the same gesture: pick a saved colour or a saved text style up off the Library shelf and carry it somewhere. Every one of their reports says the same thing to you, that no scripted walk can prove the pick-up itself, only what happens once something is in the air, and asks you to check by hand. That is three features handing the same risk to the person who is meant to be trying them. Settle it once.
notes:
Filed by the 2026-09-09 triage pass, reading the day's audits as a user.

The same paragraph appears in queue/audits/2026-09-09-text-style-drag.json, 2026-09-09-text-style-row-drop.json and, by reference, 2026-09-09-style-on-a-copy.json: "AppKit only begins a drag session from an event that came off a real device, so the walk hands the payload to the canvas directly instead... If the tile will not come away in your hand, say so and it is a small fix."

What IS already proven, so this is narrower than it sounds. Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PanelTarget.swift:12 says the harness uses "the SAME drag payload its own onDrag hands over, one closure, used by both", so the bytes on the pasteboard are the real ones. PlaytestHarness.dragTile (line 3136) then builds a PlaytestDraggingInfo and calls draggingEntered/draggingUpdated/performDragOperation on the destination. So the receiving half and the payload are covered; what nothing exercises is the mouse-down on the tile turning into a drag session.

Worth trying before concluding it is impossible: a CGEvent posted to the HID event tap is treated as a real device event, which is how other UI test harnesses start drags. Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PlaytestHarness.swift already imports CGEvent for keys.
acceptance: It is proven, and written down, that a Library tile can be picked up with a real mouse in the running app: a colour tile and a text style tile at least
Either a walk can start a real drag from now on, or the report says plainly that it cannot and names the one manual check that stands in for it
The audits that carry the warning are amended, or a line in the harness doc says where the answer lives, so the next three features do not each ask again
If the pick-up is broken for any tile, that is filed as its own bug with what was seen

log.note: Adversarial review before building. The three audits ask one question, so the shortest thing that answers it is one step that presses a tile and says whether a drag came of it, plus one walk per kind of tile. Deliberately NOT built: a general real-mouse drag framework. dragTile already covers the receiving half well and fast, and driving a whole drag with HID events would move the person's own cursor and need an Accessibility grant nobody has given. The deliverable is as much words as code: the answer has to land where the next three features will look for it.

ANSWER: a tile DOES come away in your hand. A press and a pull posted at the tile makes SwiftUI ask AppKit for a drag session; the ask is caught, recorded and refused, which is the proof and also means the step never changes the document. Colour tile comes away carrying com.photonz.paint, text style tile carrying com.photonz.text-style.

Nearly filed a false p1. The text style tile failed while the colour tile passed in the same walk, which read exactly like a broken tile. The control that saved it: picking the COLOUR tile up a second time in the same walk fails the same way. The app starts no second drag after the first, whatever the tile. Both tiles are fine; the limit is the harness's. It is now written at the top of PlaytestTilePickUp.swift, said out loud by the step when it happens, and the reason there are two walks instead of one.

Flaky until the pointer arrived first: firing a press at a tile out of nowhere came away about two times in three. A mouseMoved onto the tile, then the pull spread over real time rather than posted in a burst, made it 10 runs green out of 10 (5 per walk).

Found while running the neighbours: text-style-walk and text-style-arming-walk each failed once in a batch with "no menu called Size", and passed alone. Not caused by this change (no shared code touched). Filed as find-out-why-a-walk-sometimes-cannot-find-the-si at p2, worded as a question, with both commands and both outputs.

A tile does come away in your hand, proven by two walks. New pickUpTile step presses a tile and pulls; it catches the moment AppKit is asked for a drag session and fails if none is. tile-comes-away-walk (colour, com.photonz.paint) and text-style-comes-away-walk (text style, com.photonz.text-style), 5 runs green each. The three 2026-09-09 audits now carry the answer instead of the apology, and docs/design/playtest-harness.md has the section they point at. No bug to file: the text style tile looked broken until the control showed the colour tile fails the same way on a second pick up, which is a one-per-app-run limit of the harness, now documented and reported as itself. Scripts/test.sh green.
